task_instance: Start an EAS Simulator session (iOS, agent-device controller) for a minimal Expo project, install a build, take a screenshot via `agent-device screenshot`, then stop the session — the skill's core deliverable of running/screenshotting a user's app on a remote cloud simulator.
blocker_detail: EAS Simulator is a paid, account-gated EAS cloud service. Even the read-only first step (`simulator:availability`) requires an authenticated Expo account: eas-cli reports 'An Expo user account is required to proceed. Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable'. Interactive `eas login` needs a browser/credentials exchange and a real Expo.dev account; the non-interactive path needs an EXPO_TOKEN secret. The safety rules for this task forbid using or searching for credentials/tokens and forbid paid/account-bound services, so the session cannot proceed past this point. No local simulator fallback applies here since the task is specifically about the cloud service.
evidence: Set up a minimal Expo project skeleton (app.json with ios.bundleIdentifier, package.json) in the work directory. `npx --yes eas-cli@latest --version` succeeded (eas-cli/24.8.0, network reachable, tool installable). `npx --yes eas-cli@latest whoami` returned 'Not logged in'. `npx --yes eas-cli@latest simulator:availability --json --non-interactive` run from the project directory returned: 'An Expo user account is required to proceed. Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable if you're using EAS CLI on CI ... Error: simulator:availability command failed.' This is the documented first required step in the skill (Prerequisites / 'Check availability first') and it cannot be passed without credentials, per the task's safety rules against acquiring/using credentials and paid/account-bound services.
